another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my child Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16, their eligibility depends on their current situation. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they stay in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me whether Alex is currently in any of the following:
- Full-time education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or equivalent)
- Approved training (not an apprenticeship)
- Or has Alex left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has left education. They're not in college or doing any courses at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex is 16 and has left education, there are still a couple of ways you might qualify for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks.

Has Alex registered with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or the Careers Service in Northern Ireland), or
- The armed services?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't signed up with any careers service or the armed forces. They just finished school and are at home right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Firstly, do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great, thank you. And does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to make sure I have the full picture.

Is Alex currently:
- Working 24 hours or more per week, or
- Receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now, and they're not getting any benefits in their own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- You meet the basic requirements: you live in the UK and Alex lives with you.
- However, since Alex is 16 and has left education or training, Child Benefit would normally stop.
- There is an exception that allows Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old registers with a **government-sponsored careers service** or the **armed services** after leaving education — but Alex hasn't done this.

**What you could do:**

If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks. Alternatively, if Alex returns to approved education or training, you could also become eligible again.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. If you have any further questions, please feel free to ask.
